query: Which author name disambiguation approaches (ORCID, algorithmic clustering, manual rules) yield the best trade-off of precision/recall for law and IR corpora?

response.query: Which author name disambiguation approaches (ORCID, algorithmic clustering, manual rules) yield the best trade-off of precision/recall for law and IR corpora?
response.answer: For law and IR corpora, algorithmic clustering often yields the best trade-off of precision/recall due to its ability to dynamically adapt to complex feature sets. Manual rules can be effective but are often less scalable. ORCID provides a reliable but less flexible approach.
